To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Newport-Ingle wood zone is a narrow belt of en-echelon folds and faults that trends southeast through Miocenepliostocene sediments of th Los Angeles basin; that below this zone, in a narrow belt, is an inferred right-slip basement fault that is presumed to follow a basement contact that separates an oceanic Catalina schist facies from a continental basement facies consisting of granitic and metamorphic rocks; that the Newport-Inge wood zone of deformation ends abruptly

the Newport-Ingle wood zone of deformation in the Los Angeles area is a Pliocene-H olocene fault which is superimposed on a Mesozoic basement fault which extends offshore to the southeast for a total distance in excess of 800 mi.
the Newport-Inglewoods zone of deformation is not the trace of an ancient subduction zone.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Newport-Ingle wood zone of deformation is not a Mesozoic subduction zone, but that it is an en echelon zone of Pliocene-Holo cene deformation which is superimposed on a Mesozoic basement subduction zone.

the Newport-Ingle- wood zone of deformation is a Pliocene-Ho-locene structure which is superimposed on a basement fault which is inferred to have been active in Cretaceous times and is presumed to have been the site of Mesozoic subduction.

a Mesozoic subduction zone, which was active for a long time, is inferred to have extended from southern British Columbia southward to Baja California and that a major segment of this zone is inferred to continue southeastward under Cenozoice sediments to a depth of at least 15,000 ft and perhaps 30,000 ft.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Newport-Inglewoods subduction zone was the last of three Mesozoic ocean-floor trenches which developed in succession along the west coast of North America, and which were the principal agents in producing the Cordilleran fold belt.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Newport-Inglewoods Zone is not a single fault but a complex of en echelon faults.
the Newport-Inglewoods fault zone, and its associated deformation, is not a subduction zone.
